doc.title: Basic Usage
doc.para:
Compilation Can be compiled with Borland C++ 5.5 or later (C++ Builder 5 or later).
Compiling requires regex++ from boost.org.
After installing regex++, compile each cpp file.
For C++ Builder, simply add all cpp files of tjs2 to the project.
Can also be compiled with gcc 3 or later (can also be compiled with 2.95, but requires fixes related to wstring).

dl.dd: Loading the header files required to use TJS2. tjsError.h contains declarations regarding TJS C++ exceptions.
Specifying the locale using setlocale. If a locale is not specified, it defaults to the "C" locale, causing conversion between Japanese narrow and wide characters to fail.
Creating the TJS2 script engine with the new operator.
Entering the try block. Since TJS2 errors are notified via exceptions, exception handling needs to be done carefully.
Declaring a variable of type tTJSVariant to receive the result of executing the script.

Executing the script using tTJS::ExecScript. The script to be executed is specified in the 1st argument. String literals are converted to wide string literals using the TJS_W macro so they can be passed as tjs_char* type. In the script, function test is defined, and the result of calling that function is returned. In this example, the result of execution is returned by the return statement and received by the result variable, but if you do not need to receive the result, neither the return statement nor the 2nd argument of tTJS::ExecScript is necessary (in that case, specify NULL for the 2nd argument). The 3rd argument of tTJS::ExecScript is the execution context, but here NULL is specified. If NULL is specified, the script is executed on the global context. The 4th argument of tTJS::ExecScript specifies the name of this script. If it is NULL, it is treated as anonymous. It should be a human-readable name.
Displaying the result. Here, tTJSVariant is cast to int type.
Catching an exception of type eTJSError.

Displaying the reason for the exception using eTJSError::GetMessage. tTJSString::c_str is used to convert the message to const tjs_char *. Since tjs_char is a wide character, %ls is specified as the conversion specifier for printf.
Releasing the TJS2 script engine. Prior to release, tTJS::Shutdown is used to shut down the TJS2 script engine.

doc.para:
Calling Functions on the TJS2 Side This explains how to call a function declared on the TJS2 side from C++. Let's rewrite the inside of the aforementioned try block as follows.
tTJSVariant result; // Variable to receive the result
tjsengine->ExecScript(
TJS_W("function test(x, y) { return x*y; }"), NULL, NULL, TJS_W("test"));
tjsengine->EvalExpression(TJS_W("test(4, 5)"), &result, NULL, NULL);
// Execute expression using tTJS::EvalExpression
printf("Result : %d\n", (int)result); // Display result
iTJSDispatch2 * global = tjsengine->GetGlobalNoAddRef();
// Get global object
tTJSVariant param[] = { 4, 5 }; // Variables to pass as parameters
tTJSVariant *p_param[] = { param + 0, param + 1 }; // Array of pointers to variables
TJS_THROW_IF_ERROR(global->FuncCall(0, TJS_W("test"), NULL, &result, 2, p_param, NULL));
// Call test as a function
printf("Result : %d\n", (int)result); // Display result
Lines 3 to 4
Declaring the function test. test is registered in global.
Line 6
Executing an expression using tTJS::EvalExpression. If performance is not strictly critical, it is easy to pass an expression as a string and receive its result like this. By the way, if it is a simple expression (such as a function declaration that does not contain other execution units), compilation results are cached to some extent, allowing fast expression evaluation from the second time onwards.
Line 11
Getting the global object. The difference between tTJS::GetGlobal and tTJS::GetGlobalNoAddRef is that the former increments the reference count of the global object, whereas the latter does not. Incrementing the reference count and decrementing it when finished means locking the object so it does not get destroyed during that time. In cases like this example where there is no concern about the global object disappearing, there is no need to manipulate the reference count, so tTJS::GetGlobalNoAddRef can be used. Also, calling Release when finished is not necessary in this case.
Lines 14 to 15
Preparing parameters to pass to the function. Since iTJSDispatch::FuncCall requires an array of pointers to tTJSVariant type as parameters to pass to the function, this kind of preparation is necessary.
Line 17
Calling function "test" using iTJSDispatch2::FuncCall. The last argument of FuncCall is the 'this' (execution context) passed to the function test, but since 'this' is not used inside test declared in this example, it is fine to specify NULL. If there is a context that should be executed, that object needs to be specified. TJS_THROW_IF_ERROR is a macro that throws an exception along with a corresponding error message if the tjs_error type result is an error.

Native Functions You can create native implementations (functions implemented in C++, etc.) and access them from the TJS2 side. Even if it is not C++, as long as the language can implement iTJSDispatch2, functions written in any language can be called, but C++ is probably the easiest.
When writing functions in C++, it is easiest to derive a class from tTJSNativeFunction (described in tjsNative.h) (however, simply implementing FuncCall of iTJSDispatch2 works as a function as well).
Let's implement a simple function that multiplies two given arguments and returns the result.
class TestFunc : public tTJSNativeFunction
{
public:
tjs_error Process(tTJSVariant *result, tjs_int numparams,
tTJSVariant **param, iTJSDispatch2 *objthis)
{
if(numparams < 2) return TJS_E_BADPARAMCOUNT; // Not enough arguments
if(!result) return TJS_S_OK; // If storing the result is not required, return as is
*result = *param[0] * *param[1]; // Calculation
return TJS_S_OK; // Return TJS_S_OK to indicate normal completion
}
};
What needs to be implemented in a class inheriting from tTJSNativeFunction is only the Process method, as shown above. The arguments of the Process method are as follows:
tTJSVariant *result
A pointer to a variable of type tTJSVariant for storing the result of the function is passed. Note that if the caller does not require a result, NULL is passed.
tjs_int numparams
The number of arguments passed to the function.
tTJSVariant **param
An array of pointers to variables of type tTJSVariant storing the arguments passed to the function.
iTJSDispatch2 *objthis
The context in which the function should be executed. Can be ignored if implementing context-independent behavior.
In order to make the native function accessible from TJS2, it must be registered with an object accessible from within TJS2. In the following example, it is registered in global under the name "test". It also actually calls that function.
iTJSDispatch2 * global = tjsengine->GetGlobalNoAddRef();
// Get global object
iTJSDispatch2 *func = new TestFunc(); // Create TestFunc object
tTJSVariant func_var(func); // Set object in tTJSVariant func_var
func->Release(); // Release func
TJS_THROW_IF_ERROR(
global->PropSet(TJS_MEMBERENSURE, TJS_W("test"), NULL, &func_var, NULL));
// Register
tTJSVariant result; // Variable to receive the result
tjsengine->EvalExpression(TJS_W("test(4, 5)"), &result, NULL, NULL);
// Execute expression using tTJS::EvalExpression
printf("Result : %d\n", (int)result); // Display result
Lines 4 to 6
Creating an object of the class TestFunc that implements the native function, and converting it to tTJSVariant type. It is converted to tTJSVariant type on line 5, and at this point tTJSVariant automatically manages the reference counter of the function object, so the function object is Released on line 6.
Lines 8 to 9
Registering the function with the name "test" in the global object. Calling iTJSDispatch2::PropSet of the global object, accompanied by the TJS_MEMBERENSURE flag to create a new member.
Lines 12 to 16
Actually calling the function and displaying the result.
